def findString(N, K):

        for i in range(K):
            edge = node + str(i)
            if edge not in visited:
                visited.add(edge)
                dfs(edge[1:])

    start_node = '0' * (N - 1)

This solution uses a depth-first search (DFS) approach to construct the de Bruijn sequence, which is a cyclic sequence in which every possible string of length N appears as a substring. The algorithm efficiently constructs the sequence by exploring all possible edges in the de Bruijn graph and ensuring each edge is visited only once. The final result is obtained by appending the starting node to the constructed sequence.
